overall_summary: Hotter-than-expected CPI and hawkish Fed talk are dominating the tape, lifting hike odds, yields, and the dollar while pressuring Bitcoin toward the low seventy-thousands. Spot ETF outflows and a large miner sale add to the supply overhang, though bank custody and stablecoin funding offer limited longer-term support. Geopolitical noise remains mixed and secondary to the rates shock for now.
key_points: Hot CPI and Fed hawks drive hike odds near 90%
Bitcoin ETFs see fourth straight day of outflows
MARA dumps over 13k BTC, plans further sales
Yields and dollar surge, weighing on risk assets
Banks advance BTC custody and stablecoin funding

items.title: Hot CPI Lifts Fed Hike Odds to 90%, BTC Tests $72.7K
items.summary: US October CPI came in at 0.4 percent month over month, hotter than the 0.3 percent expected, and core also ran warm. That pushed December Fed rate-hike odds to around 90 percent on CME FedWatch. Bitcoin dipped as low as about 72,700 dollars on the print before stabilizing near 74,000. Traders should care because higher-for-longer rates tighten liquidity and have been a clear headwind for crypto risk assets.
items.impact: Near-term pressure on BTC and alts via higher real yields

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $95M for Fourth Straight Day
items.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost another 95 million dollars on Tuesday, extending the outflow streak to four sessions, with BlackRock IBIT alone accounting for 78 million. November month-to-date outflows now sit near 1.6 billion dollars. This matters because ETF flows have been the dominant institutional demand channel, and persistent redemptions remove a key bid while price sits near key moving averages.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure and weaker institutional support

items.title: Crypto Liquidations Surge to $725 Million After CPI
items.summary: Futures liquidations jumped 288 percent to roughly 725 million dollars in 24 hours as the hot inflation data hit, with the bulk coming from long positions. Open interest slipped while volume rose, showing traders cutting exposure. Watch this closely because forced selling can accelerate downside but a clean flush often leaves the market less crowded for the next move.
items.impact: Volatility spike; potential short-term washout before direction resolves

items.title: Deutsche Bank Launches Bitcoin and Ether Custody
items.summary: Germany’s largest bank has gone live with crypto custody for paying institutional and corporate clients, covering Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDC, EURC and EURAU after a long BaFin process. The service starts in Europe under MiCA with Asia expansion eyed for 2027. This is notable institutional infrastructure progress that could ease onboarding for traditional finance capital into crypto.
items.impact: Positive long-term adoption signal for regulated institutional access

items.title: MARA Sells 13,597 BTC for $1.1B, Plans More Sales
items.summary: Bitcoin miner MARA Holdings sold 13,597 BTC after the third quarter for about 1.1 billion dollars at an average near 81,000, using 750 million to fully repay its bitcoin-backed loans. The company said it intends to keep selling coins to fund AI infrastructure, convertible note puts and possible buybacks. Traders should note the extra supply from a major holder and the shift away from pure HODL strategy.
items.impact: Incremental sell pressure and miner treasury liquidation risk

items.title: Goldman, Citi Lead $270M Bank Stablecoin Funding
items.summary: A consortium of 21 banks including Goldman Sachs, Citi, Santander and Deutsche Bank has committed about 270 million dollars to fund five years of operations for a planned US dollar stablecoin issuer known as Project Faro. The group targets a first-half 2027 launch with a later euro version. This shows traditional finance building competitive stablecoin rails that could deepen on-chain liquidity and payments infrastructure.
items.impact: Constructive for crypto rails and institutional stablecoin competition

items.title: October CPI Hotter Than Expected at 0.4%
items.summary: US consumer prices rose zero point four percent month over month in October, beating the zero point three percent forecast, while core CPI also came in hot at zero point three percent versus zero point two percent expected. This is the third straight month of sticky core readings, and year over year figures were limited by last year's data gaps. Traders should care because it locks in higher odds of a December Fed hike and keeps inflation concerns front and center for risk assets.
items.impact: Raises rate-hike bets, pressures crypto and equities via tighter financial conditions

items.title: Fed's Waller Opens Door to 50bp December Hike
items.summary: Governor Christopher Waller said ahead of the CPI print that he backs a twenty-five basis point hike in December but would consider a full half-point move if core inflation hit zero point three percent or higher. The data landed exactly there, and markets quickly priced higher odds of a larger move. Crypto traders need to watch this because an upsized hike would tighten liquidity faster and typically weigh on Bitcoin.
items.impact: Increases chance of aggressive tightening, negative for risk assets

items.title: Multiple Fed Officials Signal More Rate Hikes Needed
items.summary: Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said the Fed needs at least two more quarter-point hikes and may move faster this winter, while Vice Chair Bowman noted inflation pressures are persisting and there is still work to do. Other speakers echoed that policy remains too accommodative. This chorus of hawkish talk after the hot CPI reinforces a higher-for-longer path that crypto markets usually dislike.
items.impact: Solidifies December hike expectations and potential further tightening

items.title: Treasury Yields Surge After Hot CPI and Fed Talk
items.summary: The two-year Treasury yield jumped roughly eighteen to nineteen basis points to around four point seven four percent, its biggest one-day move in months, while the ten-year climbed about twelve basis points toward five percent. Bond markets are closed today for Veterans Day after the selloff. Higher yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like Bitcoin and tighten financial conditions across the board.
items.impact: Higher discount rates and stronger dollar headwinds for crypto

items.title: US Dollar Index Climbs Above 102 on Rate Bets
items.summary: The dollar index rose about half a percent to the one hundred two point two to one hundred two point five area as traders priced in firmer Fed policy. A stronger greenback makes dollar-denominated crypto more expensive for foreign buyers and often correlates with risk-off flows. Watch DXY for confirmation of whether the post-CPI move extends.
items.impact: Dollar strength typically weighs on Bitcoin and other risk assets

items.title: Bonds Closed for Veterans Day; PPI Due Friday
items.summary: US stock markets are open for a normal session today but the Treasury market is fully closed for the federal holiday, leaving thinner liquidity and no fresh yield prints. No major data is out Wednesday; next up are jobless claims Thursday and the October PPI on Friday. Traders should stay alert for any spillover from yesterday's inflation shock into today's equity session and the upcoming producer-price report that could further shape Fed odds.
items.impact: Quieter bond reference today; PPI next key inflation catalyst

items.title: Russia-Ukraine Agree Large POW Swap in Abu Dhabi Talks
items.summary: US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine resumed in Abu Dhabi after a nine-month gap, with both sides calling the first sessions constructive. Officials say they have agreed a large prisoner-of-war exchange, potentially one thousand or more each side, with numbers to be finalized soon. Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff mediated; security guarantees and humanitarian steps were also discussed while fighting continues. Traders should care because any credible de-escalation path reduces a major geopolitical risk premium and supports risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Supports risk-on sentiment and lower volatility premium

items.title: Trump Says Iran War Militarily Over, Keeps Blockade
items.summary: President Trump declared the Iran war militarily effectively over after meeting Qatar's prime minister, saying further major strikes look unlikely for now while the US stays locked and loaded. He is maintaining the naval blockade and status quo at the request of Gulf partners even as Iran denies talks and demands are unmet. Oil markets had priced some de-escalation hopes. Crypto traders watch this closely because a true wind-down would ease energy costs and risk-off pressure, but the unresolved Hormuz situation keeps uncertainty high.
items.impact: Mixed de-escalation signal with lingering energy risk

items.title: Hormuz Tanker Attacks Continue as Oil Rebounds
items.summary: Oil steadied and rebounded from two-month lows after fresh reports of tankers hitting mines or being struck in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran saying vessels used unauthorized routes. October saw the highest monthly attack tally of the war and November incidents continue, keeping commercial traffic far below normal. Trump’s pause on new strikes had pushed prices lower, but shipping risk is blunting those hopes. Higher or sticky oil prices raise inflation fears and can pressure risk assets, so this remains a key daily watch for crypto markets.
items.impact: Elevates energy costs and risk-off pressure

items.title: China Extends Rare Earth and Trade Control Pause
items.summary: China announced a two-month extension of its suspension on expanded rare earth, battery material and related export controls, pushing the deadline to mid-January. The move forms part of broader tariff and countermeasure pauses tied to US-China talks ahead of the APEC summit. This avoids an immediate supply-chain shock for tech, EVs and defense industries. For markets it reduces a major trade-war cliff risk and is modestly supportive for global risk appetite and related equities that often correlate with crypto.
items.impact: Eases supply-chain and trade-war risk premium

items.title: Treasury Secretary Bessent Moved Over Iran Threats
items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has relocated from his Washington home to a military base after Iranian threats against his life, according to multiple reports. Bessent leads the economic pressure campaign and blockade aimed at collapsing Iran’s finances. Other top officials have already been living on bases for security. This underscores that despite talk of the war being over, targeted threats and hybrid risks remain active, which can keep a geopolitical risk premium in markets.
items.impact: Highlights unresolved Iran threat and official vulnerability

items.title: US Pulls Aircraft From Second UK Base on Iran Threat
items.summary: The United States moved more than a dozen refueling tankers and other aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in Britain amid reported Iranian threats, raising force protection levels. This follows an earlier withdrawal of bombers from another UK base after a suspected Iran-linked plot. British officials say bases remain safe while US sources link the moves to Iran. It signals that Iranian retaliation or plotting risks are still being taken seriously even as Trump talks of status quo, adding to near-term uncertainty for risk assets.
items.impact: Signals persistent Iranian threat to Western assets
